description: Authentication (identity verification), Authorization (access permission), and Accounting (tracking user activity).
Attribute-Based Access Control - Grants access dynamic privileges based on user, environmental, and resource attributes.
Access Control List - Rules defined on firewalls, routers, or file systems permitting or denying traffic/access.
Active Directory - Microsoft central directory service managing user domain authentication and network privileges.
Discretionary Access Control - Access model where the resource owner grants permissions at their own discretion.
Identity and Access Management - Policies and systems managing digital user identities and access control.
Identity Provider - System storing and managing digital identities used for user authentication in single sign-on.
Mandatory Access Control - Strict security label/clearance access control model managed solely by the system OS.
Multifactor Authentication - Security process requiring 2+ distinct verification factors before granting system access.
Privileged Access Management - Dedicated controls vaulting, monitoring, and auditing administrative accounts.
Role-Based Access Control - Access control model assigning user privileges based on defined enterprise job roles.
Single Sign-On - Authentication scheme enabling access to multiple systems with one set of login credentials.
Time-Based One-Time Password - Temporary algorithmic passcode generated from a shared secret and current time.
User Account Control - Windows feature enforcing administrative elevation prompts before running software with high privileges.
Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service - Centralized network authentication and accounting server protocol.
Terminal Access Controller Access-Control System Plus - Cisco proprietary protocol encrypting AAA communications.
Extensible Authentication Protocol - Universal authentication framework commonly utilized in 802.1X wireless networks.
EAP-Transport Layer Security - Highly secure mutual authentication mechanism utilizing digital certificates on client and server.
Challenge-Handshake Authentication Protocol - Secure remote access authentication using three-way challenge-response hashing.
Password Authentication Protocol - Legacy, insecure authentication protocol sending passwords in cleartext.
Protected Extensible Authentication Protocol - Encapsulates EAP inside an encrypted TLS tunnel for secure authentication.
Personal Identity Verification - Federal government smart card credential for physical and logical access.
Common Access Card - US Department of Defense smart card supporting multifactor authentication and PKI encryption.
Fast Identity Online - Open authentication standards utilizing public key cryptography to eliminate passwords.
File Integrity Monitoring - Security tool tracking baseline changes to operating system files and configuration settings.
